items.t: Black-Owned Transportation Company Keeps Magic City Classic Rolling For Nearly 20 Years
items.x: An Atlanta-based, Black-owned transportation company is carrying on a decades-long family legacy while helping thousands of football fans attend one of the nation’s largest HBCU sporting events, Magic City Classic, AL.com reports. For 18 years, Vectour Group has provided shuttle services for Birmingham, Alabama’s Magic City Classic, the annual football rivalry between Alabama A&M University and Alabama State University. Led by Reginald Haslam Jr., the company’s president and CEO, Vectour Group transports more than 13,000 attendees annually, according to the outlet. Founded in the late 1970s by Reggie Haslam Sr., the company grew from a transportation operation he managed while working another full-time job into a business serving major entertainment and sporting events. items.t: 81% Of Job Seekers Rejected Without Human Contact
items.x: More than 80% of U.S. job seekers have experienced rejectio n without speaking to an interviewer, according to a new survey highlighting growing frustration with hiring practices as artificial intelligence transforms recruitment , Fast Company reports . The 2026 Greenhouse Future of Hiring Candidate Report , released Oct. 20, found that 81% of American respondents had been rejected from at least one position without speaking to a human recruiter or AI interviewer in the past year. Nearly one-third, or 31%, said it happened frequently, compared with 38% of Generation Z applicants. The findings highlight mounting challenges for workers navigating an increasingly automated hiring process. Even landing an interview does not guarantee further communication, with 45% of interviewed candidates reporting that prospective employers stopped responding. items.t: Black Native Americans: The History Of A Shared & Complicated Legacy
items.x: Source: Photo by APIC/Bettmann/Getty Images Black Native Americans have always existed, yet their history remains one of the most overlooked and frequently misunderstood chapters of American history. Their stories are woven into the history of Indigenous nations, the transatlantic slave trade, colonialism, resistance, and the fight for freedom. But how did people of African descent become part of Native American tribes between the 1600s and 1800s? The answer is far more complex than many people realize. According to the National Museum of the American Indian, Black and Indigenous identities are not mutually exclusive. Black Native Americans are Indigenous peoples of the Americas and the Caribbean, as well as descendants of Indigenous peoples of Africa. items.t: Trump Cancels Campaign Appearances In Kansas And Iowa. Wait, Nevermind
items.x: Source: Andrew Harnik / Getty You know what’s funny about President Donald Trump? But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title

Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Updated traffic pattern for Meal Box pick up
items.x: STATESBORO, Ga. (WSAV) — The Food Bank has a new on-site traffic pattern so they can serve more than 1,000 families each week, effective immediately, the Food Bank released. The new changes include a new entrance, designated queuing, the meal box will be delivered to your car, exit only onto Miller Street and on-site guidance to assist drivers. Executive Director Sheila Stewart-Leach says this new traffic pattern is to help ensure a quicker pick-up experience. "Serving over 1,000 families every single week requires precision, care, and above all, safety," said Stewart-Leach. "This new traffic plan is built to handle our expanded volume smoothly, making the experience quicker and safer for our neighbors receiving support, our volunteers, and the surrounding community." New traffic pattern map. You can check out the Food Bank website to see the updates on the new map.

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.x: Nationwide Tia Tate made history in 2023 when she became the first Black woman hired as a firefighter by the Killeen Fire Department in Texas. A Killeen native, she now serves the community where she grew up. Her path to the profession began after a traumatic experience made her realize she wanted the skills to help people during emergencies. The Killeen Fire Department, established in 1920, had never hired a Black female firefighter before Tate joined its ranks. A 2012 graduate of Killeen High School, she said returning to serve her hometown made the achievement especially meaningful. However, she did not initially realize she was breaking a barrier. Her family is seeking answers about the incident, which happened while she was in the care of a babysitter who allegedly took her there without her mother's permission. Her mother, Peandra Hinton, said she did not know her daughter had been taken to the pumpkin patch. She also said the toddler was with a group of people she did not know. The circumstances surrounding the outing have left the family with questions about how the child ended up in the path of the vehicle and what happened before the collision. According to KWTX , the Sevier County Sheriff's Office said Nyxailia fell and was struck by a car driven by a family friend. items.x: Nationwide Dr. Richard E. Holmes, who was the first African American student at Mississippi State University, has died at 82. The Starkville native made history by breaking a racial barrier at the university in 1965. He later built a career in medicine before returning to the university to care for its students. His arrival came during a period when racial segregation and resistance to integration remained widespread across Mississippi. He continued his studies at the university, earning a liberal arts degree in 1969 and a master’s degree in microbiology in 1973, according to WLBT . The city has renamed Beacon Street as Kitty Black Perkins Boulevard to recognize her role in making the iconic doll more representative of Black girls. Officials unveiled the new street sign Tuesday, celebrating a career that helped change the face of Barbie. Growing up in Spartanburg’s Highland neighborhood, Perkins rarely saw dolls that looked like her. She recalled playing with paper dolls and coloring them to match her skin tone. Those childhood experiences later shaped her desire to create toys that reflected the children who played with them. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said

items.t: Upstate vape shop robbed at knifepoint
items.x: GREENVILLE COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) Deputies are searching for a woman they said robbed a vape shop at knifepoint. According to the Greenville County Sheriff's Office, deputies were called around 9:57 p.m. Friday to Smoking Joe's Vape Shop on Poinsett Highway for reports of a robbery. The sheriff's office said a black woman wearing a blue shirt and blue sweatpants entered the shop armed with a knife and demanded merchandise. While the woman was taking items from store shelves, a store employee reportedly tried to confront her, resulting in a cut on the employee's hand. The employee received medical care at the scene and is expected to recover. Anyone with information regarding the robbery is asked to contact the Greenville County Sheriff's Office.

items.t: One dead in Pickens County crash
items.x: PICKENS COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) One person was killed after a car overturned in a crash in Pickens County, according to the South Carolina Highway Patrol. Officials said they were called out to a crash on SC 11 near Roy F. Jones Highway in Pickens County. A Lexus was traveling south on SC-11, when the driver crossed the center line before going off the left side of the roadway. The vehicle then struck an embankment and overturned. The Pickens County Coroner's Office said 84-year-old Mylla Fisk Markland, of Irmon, was pronounced dead at the scene. A passenger was flown by helicopter to Prisma Health Greenville Memorial Hospital. Their condition is unknown. The incident remains under investigation by the South Carolina Highway Patrol.

items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said

items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. Many of the billed injections were either provided for cosmetic purposes only or were given to patients whose primary care physicians had not referred them for treatment of chronic migraines. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: (FOX40.COM) ICE has responded after Sacramento's city manager instructed local police not to act as "a security detail" for ICE agents. Earlier this week, a man was detained by ICE agents less than a mile from a south Sacramento elementary school. On Thursday, Sacramento City Councilmember Rick Jennings shared a post saying he is "appalled" after ICE allegedly detained a person in the Greenhaven-Pocket area.

From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said

items.t: Shelby County early vote totals up 52% this year over 2022
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. — More than 183,000 people in Shelby County cast ballots during early and absentee voting, which ended Thursday, a 52% increase over 2022. All West Tennessee counties surrounding Shelby saw increases in turnout over 2022, though most were slightly behind the early and absentee turnout for the 2018 elections. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Javits Was Supposed to Be Here
items.x: Eight years after Junior, the Bronx is burying another 15-year-old. "Crime is down" is not an answer. I walked the same Bronx streets that Javits Frimpong walked. Throughout my teenage years, I understood that my life could be in danger at any moment, or that my freedom could be threatened by a choice I might be forced to make. When you grow up surrounded by that reality and survive it, something dangerous can happen: You begin to normalize it. The sickness that has eaten at our communities is not who we are. We are worth something. Life is worth living. items.t: Cerina Fairfax's sister calls for divorce law reform six months after former Virginia lieutenant governor killed her

Six months after Dr. Cerina Fairfax was killed by her estranged husband , former Virginia Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax, her family is still struggling to make sense of the tragedy. Now, her sister is calling for changes to Virginia's divorce laws , hoping other families can avoid similar heartbreak. In an emotional interview with NBC Washington , Arisce Wanzer remembered her sister as a devoted mother, successful dentist and the person everyone in their family could count on. “We could have never imagined it would end like this,” Wanzer said, speaking from her home in Australia. On April 16, police say Justin Fairfax, 47, fatally shot his wife, 49, inside their Annandale, Virginia, home before taking his own life. Their two teenage children were home at the time, and their son called 911.

Nearly four decades after making her daytime television debut, Tamara Tunie finally has an Emmy to call her own, and she made sure to share the moment with the women who helped make it possible. The 67-year-old actress won her first-ever Emmy Award Friday night (Oct. 30), taking home Outstanding Lead Performer in a Daytime Drama Series: Actress for her portrayal of Anita Williams Dupree on CBS’ “Beyond the Gates.” For Tunie, who began her daytime career in 1987 on “As the World Turns,” the victory marked a particularly meaningful homecoming. “This is the best welcome back to daytime ever,” she declared during her acceptance speech. Prosecutors allege that a March 2021 filing declared zero taxable income, despite Guobadia allegedly knowing he had earned more. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. Officers were dispatched to the single-vehicle crash scene at 6:36 a.m. The home was unoccupied when it was hit, police said. The driver was transported to the hospital for treatment. Police did not state the extent of their injuries. This is an ongoing investigation. Continue to check WAVY.com for updates .

items.t: Senatobia Police Department damaged in fire
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. The Senatobia Police Department in Mississippi caught fire early Saturday morning, according to the Senatobia Fire Department. Fire crews say they responded to the police department a little after 4:30 a.m. due to smoke in the building. They say they were able to quickly knock down the flames and ventilate the building. City of Senatobia Fire Department City of Senatobia Fire Department At this time, it is still unclear what caused the fire, if anyone was injured, or the cost of the damage. Despite the damage to the building, the department says it is continuing to operate, provide police services without interruption, and public safety remains unaffected. Stick with WREG as we work to gather more information.

items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year.
