items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: After 65 years, Freedom Riders finally complete their journey to New Orleans
items.x: Multiple generations of Black civil rights activists met at Xavier University on Wednesday to honor a group of Freedom Riders after they finally completed a disrupted bus journey from Washington D.C. to New Orleans 65 years after the original trip was halted. The original ride, the first in a series of trips to protest Jim Crow laws, was interrupted when a segregationist mob firebombed their buses in Anniston, Alabama on May 14, 1961. The 13 riders were able to escape the bus before it exploded but sustained beatings from the mob. The next day, they flew directly to New Orleans and sought refuge at Xavier University after hotels refused to host them out of fears of further violence. Leaving D.C. on Oct. 17 and stopping in historical cities like Selma and Jackson, the latest cohort of Freedom Riders completed the bus route their predecessors were unable to. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Appeals court rules against Trump — again — on California ballots
items.x: ( The Hill ) A split federal appeals court panel again rejected the Trump administration's bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots it says are likely noncitizens until they can be verified. The 2-1 majority on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit didn’t dispute a lower court’s finding that the list isn’t credible and ruled the administration’s position would undermine the Constitution. “As the district court found—and we discern no clear error—there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the majority wrote in its unsigned opinion. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Looking back: Historic Halloween snowstorm of 1993
items.x: YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WKBN) – Halloween is known for its tricks and treats, but here in the Youngstown area, late October weather can sometimes bring a few surprises of its own. One memorable example is Halloween 1993, when a record 5.1 inches of snow fell at the Youngstown airport. A cold wind signaled the beginning of the storm Oct. 29 before the snow stole the headlines. Two days before Halloween, an unseasonably cold arctic air mass was building in the Northern Plains, rushing toward the western Great Lakes, with Youngstown right on the edge of the cold front. Cold air builds in the Northern Plains on October 29, 1993 moving towards Youngstown. (Image: NOAA Archive Library) By the time Halloween arrived, the cold air mass moved down to the Gulf Coast, with Youngstown in the heart of some of the coldest air in the country. items.t: Salem restaurant to close after 30 years
items.x: SALEM, Ohio (WKBN) It's been an emotional day for a local family as it opened its doors to the community for one last time. Friday marked the final day of operations for Adele's Place in Salem, as owner Adele Lake is riding off into retirement. She's been working at the restaurant for over 50 years and has been the owner for the last 30. They have their regular customers, who spoke about how they've watched the family grow over the years. Many filed in on their final day for one last meal. "If you could have been here all this week, you couldn't get in the door. The parking lot was packed," Lake said. "The bread man couldn't even deliver his bread. He had to drop it off and leave. That's how busy we were. They have supported 100% since the day I opened." Lake says she's not sure what she will do with her time now, but says she will figure it out.

Shapiro was joined by State Senator James Malone (D), who flipped a red seat during a 2025 special election. The governor believes Malone's seat and five other State Senate seats are in play this year, but is optimistic Tuesday night "will be a good night" for Democrats. "I'm optimistic about all these races," Shapiro told reporters. "I think it's important to note that all those State Senate districts are really, really gerrymandered. It's really tough." items.t: Mercer County veterans honored at appreciation breakfast
items.x: HERMITAGE, Pa. (WKBN) An appreciation breakfast was held Friday morning in Mercer County at the VFW Hall. The event was started by Pennsylvania State Representative Parke Wentling to honor those who served and are currently serving our country. Pennsylvania Congressman Mike Kelly says the event has gone beyond anything he and Wentling ever imagined. "You feel it in the room. This is not a political event, which is really nice for a change to just go to something. We are honoring those who served and have put their lives on the line, the true 1% of American citizens," Kelly said. "To have an event like this and see all these veterans show up, it is so gratifying to be able to thank them for everything they've done." Kelly added that events like these help remind everyone that it is our veterans that made things safe for everyone and that it was an honor to spend the morning with them.

But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." 📧 Have breaking news come to you: Subscribe to News 2 email alerts → “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.x: ( NerdWallet ) I get groceries delivered about three times a month. From my couch, I can also order dinner, buy a dress for an upcoming wedding and stream a movie. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . According to Schefter, multiple teams have reached out to the Colts and talks are active and ongoing. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Indianapolis Zoo’s collections and veterinary employees vote to unionize
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS— An announcement on Thursday detailed that the Indy Zoo's collections and veterinary employees had voted to unionize. In a statement posted to Facebook , the Indiana-Kentucky district of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees welcomed workers at the Indianapolis Zoo to its organization. The AFSCME began in 1932 and is one of the largest union organizations in the United States. The Indianapolis Zoo sent a statement reacting to the announcement that read, in part, "of course, the Zoo is disappointed in this result, but at this time, it is reviewing the election results and the Zoo’s potential legal options in advance of their official certification by the National Labor Relations Board." The local AFSCME chapter will be the bargaining representative for the unionized employees. It is unclear at this time when those negotiations are set to take place.

items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: St. Louis Fire Captain honored for emergency fix to damaged fire hydrants
items.x: ST. LOUIS St. Louis Fire Captain Bradley Trower is being honored for his quick thinking skills and ingenuity after damage to dozens of fire hydrants. Investigators say at least one suspect stole brass valves from hydrants to sell as scrap metal, leaving them inoperable. Trower developed an emergency adapter practically overnight that allows firefighters to connect their hoses to damaged hydrants and access water. "It's not a perfect system. It still leaks, but it does flow enough water for our apparatus to operate," said Trower. Mayor Cara Spencer and Fire Chief Dennis Jenkerson recognized Trower with an "Excellence in Service" award for his innovative solution. Earlier this month, police arrested one suspect believed to be responsible for the hydrant thefts.

items.t: David Dorn Foundation donates safety lights to Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office
items.x: JEFFERSON COUNTY, Mo. The Captain David Dorn Foundation donated "Guardian Angel Safety Lights" to the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office on Friday. The equipment is designed to improve visibility and safety during overnight operations and high-risk situations. "If we're directing traffic, even with the vest on, that strobing light is just one more thing that grabs someone's attention," said Deputy Zachary Reed. " Oh hey, there's someone there. There's actually something moving right there.' And that movement catches people's eyes a little bit faster when there might be a lot of emergency scene lighting or other vehicles moving around." The foundation honors the legacy of fallen St. Louis Police Captain David Dorn, who was killed in the line of duty during anti-police riots in 2020.

items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Historic polar vortex disruption could influence Midwest weather late this year
items.x: ST. LOUIS Meteorologists are closely watching what could become one of the earliest major Sudden Stratospheric Warming (SSW) events on record. Forecast models are indicating a dramatic weakening, and possibly a temporary reversal of winds high above the Arctic during the first half of November. If the event occurs as predicted, it could disrupt the polar vortex weeks earlier than is typically observed during the northern hemisphere winter. What is a Sudden Stratospheric Warming? A Sudden Stratospheric Warming occurs when temperatures rapidly increase in the stratosphere, roughly 20 to 30 miles above the Earth's surface. This warming can weaken or even split the polar vortex the ring of strong winds that normally helps contain Arctic air near the North Pole. items.t: Advocates warn of increase in animal activity on Virginia roads following end of daylight saving time
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) Daylight saving time ending means turning the clocks back and getting an extra hour of sleep, but with earlier sunsets come more crashes on Virginia roadways involving animals. There are 28% more nighttime crashes and a 16% increase in deer collisions in the week after daylight saving time ends, according to the nonprofit organization Environment America . "This time of day we now will be travelling home from work or school or from sports or whatever, is when animals are actually most active," said Elly Wilson, Environment Virginia State Director. The time change coincides with deer breeding season, or rut. “They’re just more active. They're more likely to dash across the road and just be out and about," Wilson said. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: (The Conversation) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: What is the ‘Couch Economy’ costing you?
items.x: (NerdWallet) I get groceries delivered about three times a month. From my couch, I can also order dinner, buy a dress for an upcoming wedding and stream a movie. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . In the couch economy era, more and more domestic spending is happening online — 58% in 2026 in the U.S., compared to 48% in 2019, based on Visa transactions. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: (NewsNation) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said Ja

items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: (NewsNation) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides, according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: (KTLA) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." items.t: UAH gets over $3M to help students prepare for college, careers
items.x: HUNTSVILLE, Ala. (WHNT) — Hundreds of north Alabama students will soon have extra support as they prepare for college and careers. The University of Alabama in Huntsville has secured a $3,231,252 federal GEAR UP grant that will serve about 700 students in Limestone and Marshall counties over the next six years. The program will provide tutoring, career planning, financial literacy and mentorship to help students succeed beyond high school. UAH says its departments will collaborate with partner schools to expand access to university resources, including recruitment and admissions guidance, dual enrollment opportunities and academic pathways.

items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its deve

items.x: ( The Hill ) A Cheesecake Factory jab from former President Obama quickly spiraled into a midterm spat between the GOP and Democrats as the competitive election cycle nears its end. Obama quipped during a recent campaign stop in Cleveland that President Trump has the White House “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory, it’s just gold everywhere.” His remarks referred to Trump’s reported $900 million renovations to the White House, including pricey updates to the Rose Garden and constructing a new granite helipad , according to the Washington Post. Hussein’s Iraqi palaces were also famously adorned with gold fixtures and decor. “We have to explain to Obama that the White House is a symbol of America, and it has to be maintained properly,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland en route to Mississippi Monday. items.t: Appeals court rules against Trump — again — on California ballots
items.x: ( The Hill ) A split federal appeals court panel again rejected the Trump administration's bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots it says are likely noncitizens until they can be verified. The 2-1 majority on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit didn’t dispute a lower court’s finding that the list isn’t credible and ruled the administration’s position would undermine the Constitution. “As the district court found—and we discern no clear error—there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the majority wrote in its unsigned opinion. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: New app turns Congress into a fantasy sports competition
items.x: AUSTIN (Nexstar) — On Tuesday night, Texans will select 35 members of Congress to represent them for the next two years. Soon after, they can add those lawmakers to fantasy teams and track how well they govern once they're in Washington. Inspired by his love of fantasy football, Houstonian-turned-Austinite Alex Kurkowski created the app RabbleRouser this year using the AI-powered tool Claude. The app allows users to draft U.S. senators and representatives who rack up points by introducing legislation, taking votes and advancing bills through Congress. "During the (NFL) offseason, there's nothing going on. So I figured, Hey, why not get into politics?'" Kurkowski said. "So I just built it starting from scratch just because of the void of fantasy football." items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Nocturnal neighbors: Austin Bat Refuge busts common misconceptions
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Millions of bats live alongside us in Central Texas. One group of experts works to rehabilitate creatures that need care and educate people about how to live alongside these nocturnal neighbors. Ahead of Halloween, Hilary Pelham with the refuge explained some of the common misconceptions about these animals. For example, none of the 10 species that live in the Austin area drink blood but rather are insectivores. "I like to say that the scariest thing about bats is what would happen if we didn't have them," she said. "That would mean agricultural collapse." She said that Mexican Free-Tailed bats, famous for emerging from under the Congress Avenue Bridge every night, eat crop pests saving billions of dollars in agricultural costs per year for farmers. items.t: Healthcare becomes key midterm issue ahead of policy changes
items.x: (DC BUREAU) – Healthcare costs could rise for insured Americans as states prepare to enforce new Medicaid restrictions in January under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The legislation, signed by President Donald Trump, requires states to enforce stricter Medicaid work requirements and mandate that enrollees reapply twice a year. The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office projects millions of Americans will lose healthcare coverage as a result of the changes. Policy analysts warn the loss of coverage will impact hospital systems. items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Westwood snapped its six-game losing streak Friday night, defeating McNeil 63-33 at Kelly Reeves Athletic Complex to earn its first District 25-6A victory of the season. The Warriors (2-7, 1-4) erupted for a season-high 63 points, surpassing their previous scoring high of 24 in their Week 2 victory over Austin High. Westwood entered Friday's matchup having been outscored 256-79 during its six-game skid. The victory marked the Warriors' first win since September and gave them momentum heading into their regular-season finale. McNeil (0-10, 0-5), meanwhile, finishes its season winless. The Mavericks struggled defensively throughout the year, entering Friday's contest allowing an average of 57.2 points per game. items.t: Austin’s Sweetest Halloween Destination Offers Candy, Curiosities & A New Supernatural Book
items.x: Halloween season is in full swing, and one Austin favorite is serving up more than just sweets. Big Top Candy Shop , located on South Congress and with a new second store in Hyde Park, is known for its incredible selection of nostalgic treats, international candies, craft sodas, and hard-to-find sweets that make it a must-visit destination this time of year. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. "Typically, with El Niño, there is a wetter winter, and near normal, to maybe slightly below normal temperatures," Christopher Bannan, National Weather Service meteorologist, said. As for the possibility of below normal temperatures, they said that doesn't necessarily mean we should expect winter weather events like we have seen in years past. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock.
